speaker: Doctor
text:
Good morning. Your history of a painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own, followed by current right knee pain and urinary symptoms, suggests a specific type of inflammatory arthritis. To confirm my suspicion, have you noticed any recent eye redness, skin rashes, or a fever? 

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, ESR, CRP, and HLA-B27.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: WBC 12–16/hpf, RBC 1–2/hpf, Protein Negative, Blood Negative; ESR 38 mm/h; CRP: Not available in provided data; HLA-B27: Not available in provided data

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history reported. Social history: Sexually active with multiple partners, inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Patient
text: Experiences anxiety; denies recent flu-like symptoms, denies any known sexually transmitted infections. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand your anxiety, but please stay calm while we wait for the lab results which will confirm our suspicion. Based on your history of self-resolving ankle swelling, current knee pain, and urinary issues, we are looking for a classic pattern of inflammatory arthritis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis.
